svg.title: Additional nonconvex comparisons at equal gradient-call budgets

cc:Work.dc:title: Additional nonconvex comparisons at equal gradient-call budgets
cc:Work.dc:description: Additional method comparison on 32-client, four-block nonconvex problems with block dimension eight, M=8, and 20 paired runs per case. All methods receive a total budget of 8000 training client-block gradient calls, including the gradient-table method's 128-call initialization; diagnostic full gradients are excluded and separately accounted for. Panels (a,b) report the budget-weighted running mean of the squared full deterministic proximal-gradient mapping: initialization calls retain the initial-state mapping, and each selected-block update is weighted by its training gradient calls. Thus the same call axis and initial-cost accounting apply to all methods. The methods are Geometric, Inverse inclusion, and the implemented client gradient-table baseline; the latter is a gradient-memory reference method. Panel (c) shows each method's final empirical objective, to be compared within each case. Lines/points are run means; bands/bars are nominal pointwise 95% Student-t confidence intervals with 19 degrees of freedom. They are not run SD or simultaneous bands; intervals describe individual method means rather than paired method differences. Data and algorithmic schedules remain paired across methods. Both cases are synthetic, use the same fixed selected-block stepsize 0.015 across methods, and include no per-method tuning. The coupled case is a stress experiment, and generated zero-tilt labels are not claims about the coupled population optimum.
